title: SQLite Quick Guide
description: Find a short explanation and a worked example for each idea in the SQLite course.

entries.name: Ask SQLite for an answer
entries.summary: SQLite can calculate a value without a table.

entries.name: Create a sample table
entries.summary: A table defines named columns for each record.

entries.name: Inspect the kind of a value
entries.summary: SQLite values have storage classes such as integer, real and text.

example.code: SELECT typeof(12) AS whole,typeof(2.5) AS decimal_kind,typeof('12') AS words;

entries.name: Filter a query-only list
entries.summary: WHERE chooses rows that pass a rule. A WITH list gives this practice query its own small dataset.

example.code:
WITH books(title,pages) AS (VALUES('Moon Trip',60),('Tiny Seed',20))
SELECT title FROM books WHERE pages>=50;

entries.name: Sort and limit the result
entries.summary: ORDER BY chooses the result order. LIMIT then keeps only the requested number of rows.

example.code:
WITH books(title,pages) AS (VALUES('Moon Trip',60),('Tiny Seed',20),('Garden Days',40))
SELECT title FROM books ORDER BY pages,title LIMIT 2;

entries.name: Count a group of rows
entries.summary: GROUP BY combines matching categories for a summary.

example.code:
WITH books(kind) AS (VALUES('story'),('science'),('story'))
SELECT kind,count(*) AS total FROM books GROUP BY kind ORDER BY kind;

entries.name: Join related records
entries.summary: A join matches records using a rule. It can show an author name beside a title without repeating that name in every book record.

example.code:
WITH authors(id,name) AS (VALUES(1,'Mia')),books(title,author_id) AS (VALUES('Moon Trip',1))
SELECT books.title,authors.name FROM books JOIN authors ON authors.id=books.author_id;

entries.name: Protect a positive number
entries.summary: A CHECK constraint gives a rule for stored data.

entries.name: Turn on foreign-key checks
entries.summary: A foreign key links a child record to a parent id.

entries.name: Undo an unfinished change
entries.summary: A transaction can group row changes. ROLLBACK cancels uncommitted work inside that transaction.

entries.name: Inspect a table definition
entries.summary: PRAGMA table_info shows facts about a table's columns.

entries.name: Bind a value from Python
entries.summary: An application should pass a value separately from SQL text.

example.code:
import sqlite3
with sqlite3.connect(":memory:") as connection:
    connection.execute("CREATE TABLE books(title TEXT)")
    connection.execute("INSERT INTO books VALUES (?)", ("Moon Trip",))
    print(connection.execute("SELECT title FROM books").fetchone()[0])
